items.title: A @CNBC guest just dismissed the doubling of the national debt in ten years because household net worth more than doubled over that time. But the debt is a permanent obligation that must be serviced and repaid. Net worth, besides being overly concentrated, is transitory as it can evaporate if rising interest rates crash over-valued stock and real estate prices.

items.title: On our national debt, the average coupon on maturities beyond ten years is 3.44%. That's way below current long-term rates. Buying that debt back now is like a homeowner refinancing a 3.44% 30-year fixed-rate mortgage into a 4% one-year ARM. Who would be dumb enough to do that?
